quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to any driver who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: When are collisions more likely to happen?

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver travels faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases crash risk. Driving slower than traffic can cause rear-end collisions or force other drivers to swerve.

questions.question: What must you do when you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe night driving practice?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your pupils contract. When the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to readjust to darker light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. Bicyclists have little protection, so do not crowd them. Passing too fast can force them off their path.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a curved downhill ramp. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Begin braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause skidding.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough for others to know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough for others to know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers know what you plan to do in advance.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to exit the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and show that road work is happening on or near the road. Drive with extra care in these areas.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: You cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
You see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
You have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane after passing, make sure you have enough space between you and the other vehicle. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to safely return to your lane.

questions.question: What is one benefit of looking far ahead while driving on the highway?

options.text: It helps you keep up with traffic.
It reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
It allows you to spot police officers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking ahead helps you avoid sudden braking or turning. When you watch the road ahead, you can prepare for stops or lane changes. This makes driving safer, saves fuel, and helps traffic move smoothly.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes in an intersection.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check if other drivers are moving into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Also check for other drivers who may be trying to enter the same lane. Never try to pass or change lanes inside an intersection.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
When the crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time from either direction. Do not cross the tracks unless your vehicle can completely clear them. Never stop your vehicle while it is on the tracks.

questions.question: How do you check for vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. To check your blind spots, you must look over your shoulders.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Always use the proper turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in foggy weather?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Never drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights when visibility is 500 feet or less. Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
It means the same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibrations to alert drowsy drivers that they have left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibrations to alert drowsy drivers that they have left the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: How do you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This round sign warns you that railroad tracks are ahead. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop for trains.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians go first.
Go faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection go first.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger instead of the road while driving.
Only watches the car in front and ignores everything else.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay focused on the road. Do not look at passengers, search for things in your car, read, sightsee, or daydream. Scan the road often, check your mirrors, and watch your dashboard regularly. These habits keep you alert and safe.

questions.question: This sign warns of a type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns that another road crosses the highway ahead.
